# Arista EOS, cEOS, and vEOS Cheat Sheet

These examples use EOS CLI on an independently obtained cEOS image; use the appropriate interface names and EOS release for your lab. cEOS and vEOS are EOS environments, but their image formats and platform capabilities differ.

## Connect and inspect

```sh
docker exec -it clab-LAB-sw Cli
```

At the EOS prompt:

```text
show version
show running-config
show interfaces status
show ip interface brief
show vlan
show lldp neighbors
show ip route
show ip ospf neighbor
show ip bgp summary
show ip bgp 203.0.113.0/24
```

Use `enable` if privileged EXEC mode is required. The `show` commands inspect state and do not change the configuration.

## Configure a routed interface

```text
enable
configure terminal
interface Ethernet1
   no switchport
   ip address 10.1.12.2/30
   no shutdown
end
show ip interface brief
```

To remove the address, enter the interface configuration and use `no ip address 10.1.12.2/30`. `write memory` saves the running configuration to startup configuration; preserve the lab's source configuration separately before destroying a container.

## VLAN checks

Use `show vlan`, `show interfaces trunk`, `show spanning-tree`, and `show mac address-table` to compare forwarding state with the diagram. Interface and feature availability depend on the image and release.
